trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Banff, Alberta, Canada
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.description: Hike the Rockpile Trail and Lakeshore Trail at Moraine Lake, one of the most photographed lakes in the world. The vivid blue glacial water set against the Valley of the Ten Peaks is an unforgettable natural spectacle.

experiences.name: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint
experiences.description: Drive the world-renowned Icefields Parkway (Highway 93) and stop at Peyto Lake viewpoint, where the wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake sits in a sweeping alpine valley. Combine with stops at Bow Lake and Crowfoot Glacier for a full day of breathtaking natural scenery.

day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00 on Flight AC. Collect luggage and take the Banff Airporter or Brewster Express shuttle (~$60-70 CAD one-way) to Banff town (~1.5 hrs). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge. Walk Banff Avenue to get oriented, pick up a Parks Canada day pass (~$10.50 CAD/person) at the Banff Visitor Centre, and grab groceries at Nesters Market for budget meal supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Bow River Falls (free, 10-min walk from town centre) for a gentle first taste of Banff's scenery. Watch the sunset over the Bow River. Return to town for a budget-friendly dinner.

meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or snack at Calgary Airport before boarding or on the shuttle.
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's on Bear Street — casual Cajun-inspired spot with affordable wraps and burgers (~$15-18 CAD). Alternatively, cook a simple pasta meal at the lodge using groceries from Nesters Market to save money.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 6-day Parks Canada Discovery Pass (~$145 CAD/adult or ~$290 family) at the Visitor Centre — it pays for itself quickly and covers all park entry fees. Download the AllTrails app and offline maps for Banff National Park tonight. Set an early alarm for Day 2 as Moraine Lake requires a very early start.

day_by_day.morning: MORAINE LAKE — Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trail. Depart hotel by 05:30 AM (critical — Moraine Lake Road closes to private vehicles after ~08:00 AM in peak season). Take the Parks Canada shuttle from Banff town (~$8 CAD return) or the Lake Louise Connector. Hike the Rockpile Trail (0.8 km, easy, ~30 min) for the iconic panoramic view of Moraine Lake and the Ten Peaks. Then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return, easy, ~1.5 hrs) hugging the brilliant turquoise shoreline. Total morning hike: ~2-3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return shuttle to Lake Louise village (~10 min). Visit Lake Louise itself (free with Parks pass) — walk the flat Lakeshore Trail (4 km return, easy, ~1 hr) along the stunning glacial lake with views of Victoria Glacier. Browse the free shoreline; skip the Fairmont canoe rentals (~$155/hr) to stay on budget. Catch the return shuttle to Banff (~45 min).
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover at the lodge. Optional short sunset walk up Tunnel Mountain Trail (4.8 km return, ~1.5 hrs, moderate) for panoramic views over Banff townsite — golden hour light is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Prepare oatmeal or granola bars at the lodge before 05:30 AM departure. Pack a travel coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from lodge groceries — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and a reusable water bottle (water is drinkable from lodge tap). Eat at Moraine Lake or Lake Louise shoreline.
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — pub-style mains like burgers and fish & chips (~$18-22 CAD). Happy hour deals available 3-5 PM. Alternatively, cook stir-fry at the lodge.

day_by_day.notes: The 05:30 AM departure is non-negotiable in July — Moraine Lake Road fills up extremely fast. Bring layers; mornings at Moraine Lake can be 8-12°C even in July. Bear spray rental (~$10/day) is recommended and available at Wilson Mountain Sports in Banff. Confirm shuttle times the evening before at the Banff Visitor Centre or pc.gc.ca.

day_by_day.morning: JOHNSTON CANYON — Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike. Drive or take a Roam Transit bus (Route 8X, ~$6 CAD return) to Johnston Canyon trailhead (~20 min from Banff). Hike the iconic canyon catwalk trail to the Lower Falls (2.7 km return, easy, ~45 min) — the metal walkways bolted into the canyon walls are dramatic and unique. Continue to the Upper Falls (5.4 km return from trailhead, easy-moderate, ~2 hrs total). For the adventurous, extend to the Ink Pots (11.6 km return, moderate, ~4 hrs total) — seven cold mineral springs in a beautiful open meadow. Total morning: 3-4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff. Visit Vermilion Lakes (free, 5 min drive or 30-min walk/cycle from town) — three shallow lakes with stunning Rundle Mountain reflections. Excellent wildlife spotting area (elk, beaver, osprey). Walk the flat 4.5 km trail along the lakes. Rent a bike from Soul Ski & Bike (~$12-15/hr) to cover more ground affordably.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free Banff Park Museum (National Historic Site, nominal entry ~$4 CAD) on Banff Avenue — a charming Victorian natural history museum. Stroll Banff Avenue for window shopping. Enjoy the warm summer evening along the Bow River Pathway.

meals.breakfast: Cook eggs and toast at the lodge before departing.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Ink Pots meadow or Johnston Canyon picnic area — wraps, cheese, crackers, and fruit.
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Bear Street — vegetarian/vegan-friendly with affordable bowls and wraps (~$14-18 CAD). Great budget option with healthy portions.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is very popular — arriving by 08:30 AM avoids the worst crowds. The catwalk can be slippery; wear grippy trail shoes. The Ink Pots extension adds ~6 km but is highly recommended for a quieter, rewarding experience. Check Roam Transit schedules at roamtransit.com — buses run frequently in summer.

day_by_day.morning: ICEFIELDS PARKWAY — Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint. Rent a car for the day (~$60-80 CAD from Enterprise or National in Banff) or join a budget group tour (~$50-70 CAD). Drive north on Highway 93 — one of the world's most scenic roads. First stop: Bow Lake (~40 min from Banff) — short flat walk to the lakeshore with Crowfoot Glacier views (free). Second stop: Peyto Lake Viewpoint (~55 min from Banff) — hike the Bow Summit Trail (1.6 km return, easy, ~30 min) to the famous wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake viewpoint. Breathtaking panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield area (~1.5 hrs from Banff). View the Athabasca Glacier from the free roadside viewpoint (skip the expensive Glacier Adventure ride ~$60+ CAD to stay on budget). Walk to the glacier toe on the free public path — read interpretive signs about glacial retreat. Stop at Sunwapta Falls (~15 min south of Icefield) — short 0.8 km walk to powerful twin waterfalls (free). Drive back south, stopping at Herbert Lake for a quiet picnic and reflection views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 18:00-19:00. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening. Walk to Cascade Gardens (free) behind the Park Administration Building for manicured gardens with Cascade Mountain backdrop — perfect golden hour photography.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast — peanut butter toast, banana, coffee from the lodge before 07:30 AM departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Bow Lake or Herbert Lake picnic area — this is essential as food options on the Parkway are very expensive ($25+ CAD at the Icefield Centre).
meals.dinner: Masala Authentic Indian Cuisine on Wolf Street — generous portions, affordable lunch/dinner specials (~$15-20 CAD). Great vegetarian options too.

day_by_day.notes: The Icefields Parkway is 230 km one-way to Jasper — today's route covers the southern highlights (~120 km to Columbia Icefield and back, ~3.5 hrs driving total). Fill up with gas in Banff before leaving — there are no stations on the Parkway until Saskatchewan Crossing (~80 km north). Bring extra water and snacks. Wildlife sightings (bears, elk, bighorn sheep) are common — never stop in the middle of the road.

day_by_day.morning: SULPHUR MOUNTAIN & HOT SPRINGS — Hike up Sulphur Mountain Trail (11 km return, moderate-strenuous, ~3-4 hrs, 655m elevation gain) starting from the Banff Gondola base station. This free hike rewards with panoramic 360° views over the Bow Valley, six mountain ranges, and Banff townsite. At the summit, explore the free boardwalk to Sanson Peak weather observatory. The views rival the gondola ride at zero cost (gondola costs ~$65 CAD — skip it!).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Sulphur Mountain and reward yourself with a soak at Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$18 CAD adult entry — the most affordable spa experience in Banff). Natural mineral hot spring pool at 37-40°C with mountain views. Towel rental available (~$2 CAD). Spend 1.5-2 hours relaxing. Afternoon stroll along the Bow River Trail (flat, paved, free) from the hot springs back toward town.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Two Jack Lake in Banff's Minnewanka area (~10 min drive from town, free with Parks pass) for a peaceful sunset walk along the lakeshore (easy 2 km loop). The calm lake reflects Mount Rundle beautifully at golden hour. Return to Banff for a final evening stroll on Banff Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Hearty lodge breakfast before the climb — oatmeal with nuts and dried fruit, hard-boiled eggs, coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Sulphur Mountain summit — enjoy sandwiches and snacks with the best view in Banff. Pack extra water (1.5L minimum for this hike).
meals.dinner: Melissa's Missteak on Lynx Street — a beloved Banff institution since 1972, known for hearty portions. Burgers and casual mains run ~$18-22 CAD. Worth the slight splurge for a memorable meal.

day_by_day.notes: Start the Sulphur Mountain hike by 07:30 AM to beat the heat and crowds. The trail is well-marked but steep in sections — trekking poles are helpful (rent at Wilson Mountain Sports ~$10/day). Bring swimwear and a small bag for the hot springs — lockers are available (~$1 coin). The hot springs close at 22:00 in summer.

day_by_day.morning: LAKE MINNEWANKA & FAREWELL HIKE — Take the free Roam Transit Route 6 (~$3 CAD) or walk/cycle (~6 km from town) to Lake Minnewanka, the largest lake in Banff National Park. Hike the Lake Minnewanka Trail along the north shore (easy-moderate, go as far as desired — first 5 km to the first viewpoint and back is ideal for a final morning hike). Crystal-clear glacial lake with dramatic mountain walls. Watch for bighorn sheep on the rocky slopes above. Optional: rent a kayak or canoe (~$30-40 CAD/hr) for a budget-friendly paddle on the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by noon. Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (store luggage if needed). Final walk through town — browse the free Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (free on Sundays, ~$10 CAD other days) for local art and history. Pick up any last souvenirs at the farmers market or affordable shops on Bear Street. Head to the shuttle stop for the Banff Airporter back to Calgary Airport (~$60-70 CAD) — book the appropriate departure time based on your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Calgary Airport. If time permits before departure, grab a final meal in Banff before the shuttle. Reflect on an incredible 6-day budget adventure in the Canadian Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — use up remaining groceries to minimize waste and save money. Make a good meal before checkout.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Minnewanka shoreline — finish remaining packed food supplies.
meals.dinner: Coyotes Southwestern Grill on Caribou Street — fresh, flavourful Southwestern cuisine with affordable lunch/early dinner options (~$16-20 CAD). Great final Banff meal. Alternatively, grab a quick affordable bite at the Banff Ave Brewing Co. before the shuttle.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Airporter shuttle in advance at banffairporter.com — allow at least 3 hours before your flight departure from Calgary (the drive is ~1.5 hrs plus check-in time). Leave Lake Minnewanka by 11:30 AM at the latest to allow comfortable checkout and shuttle time. Double-check Parks Canada pass and any rental returns. The Discovery Pass makes a great souvenir — it's valid for 12 months from first use if you plan to return to Canadian national parks.

trip_options.title: Classic Banff, Alberta, Canada Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Hike the iconic Plain of Six Glaciers trail above Lake Louise, offering stunning views of Victoria Glacier and turquoise alpine waters. Optionally rent a canoe on the lake for a serene paddle surrounded by towering peaks.

experiences.description: Ride the Banff Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres for panoramic views of six mountain ranges. Walk the 1 km summit boardwalk to Sanson Peak and explore the interpretive centre about the region's ecology and history.

experiences.name: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike
experiences.description: Walk the dramatic canyon catwalk trail through Johnston Canyon to the Lower and Upper Falls, carved through limestone over thousands of years. Extend the hike to the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs with vivid blue-green pools in an open meadow.

experiences.name: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint
experiences.description: Drive the world-renowned Icefields Parkway (Highway 93) and stop at Peyto Lake viewpoint, where the wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake sits in a sweeping alpine valley. Combine with stops at Bow Lake and Crowfoot Glacier for a full day of breathtaking natural scenery.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight AC arrives at 14:00. Travel time from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge is approximately 1.5 hours. Relax and enjoy the scenic Trans-Canada Highway drive through the Rockies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge upon arrival (~15:30). Freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented. Walk down to the Bow River and cross the bridge to Central Park for a gentle, relaxing introduction to the town and mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Browse local shops along Banff Avenue, then head to the Cave and Basin National Historic Site viewpoint area for a short sunset walk along the Marsh Loop trail (free, 30 minutes). Wind down with dinner nearby.

meals.lunch: Grab a bite at the Calgary airport before departure or pick up snacks at a gas station en route to Banff.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace on Bear Street — mid-range Canadian cuisine featuring locally sourced bison and Rocky Mountain ingredients. Budget ~$35–50 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pick up your Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the Banff Visitor Centre (224 Banff Ave) if you haven't already — it covers park entry fees and saves money over 6 days. Confirm your hotel parking situation upon check-in. Light packing for the evening walk is all you need.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — Depart the hotel by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Drive ~25 minutes west on the Trans-Canada to Johnston Canyon. Walk the dramatic canyon catwalk trail through the carved limestone gorge to the Lower Falls (1.1 km one way) and continue to the Upper Falls (2.7 km one way). The cool canyon air and turquoise cascades make this a magical morning hike. Allow 2.5–3 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, drive back toward Banff and stop at Vermilion Lakes for a scenic lakeside picnic with iconic Mt. Rundle reflections. Spend 45 minutes exploring the lakeshore. Return to the hotel to freshen up, then ride the Sulphur Mountain Gondola (depart ~2:00 PM) to 2,281 metres for panoramic views of six mountain ranges. Walk the Summit Boardwalk to the Sanson's Peak meteorological station. Allow 2–2.5 hours including gondola ride.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Gondola tickets: ~$65 CAD per adult. Book online in advance to secure your time slot.
day_by_day.evening: Descend from Sulphur Mountain and relax at the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$20 CAD) for a well-earned soak with mountain views — a perfect way to ease tired legs after a full hiking day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab a coffee and pastry at Whitebark Café on Bear Street before heading out.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from Nesters Market (grocery store on Marten Street) — sandwiches, fruit, and trail snacks to enjoy at Vermilion Lakes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tooloulou's on Banff Avenue — a lively Cajun-inspired mid-range restaurant with hearty portions. Budget ~$25–40 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Start early for Johnston Canyon — the parking lot fills by 9:00 AM in peak summer. Consider taking the Banff Roam Transit bus (Route 1X) to the canyon if you prefer to avoid driving and parking stress. Wear layers; the canyon is noticeably cooler than town.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake — Valley of the Ten Peaks Trail. Depart hotel by 7:00 AM (CRITICAL: Moraine Lake Road requires a Parks Canada shuttle reservation or early arrival — no private vehicles after ~6:30 AM peak season). Take the Parks Canada shuttle from the Lake Louise Ski Area park-and-ride (~$8 CAD return). Upon arrival, hike the Rockpile Trail (20 minutes, easy) for the iconic panoramic view of Moraine Lake and the Ten Peaks. Then hike the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return, easy) along the brilliant turquoise shoreline. Allow 3–3.5 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the shuttle back to the Lake Louise Ski Area, then drive 15 minutes to Lake Louise village. Begin the Lake Louise Hike & Canoe experience — hike the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (14 km return, moderate) starting from the lakeshore. The trail climbs above Lake Louise offering breathtaking views of Victoria Glacier and the surrounding peaks. Hike as far as the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (~5.5 km from the lake) for a natural turnaround point. Allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff (~1 hour drive). Relax at the hotel before a well-deserved dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a grab-and-go option — you need to be on the road by 7:00 AM.
meals.lunch: Stop at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (open seasonally, cash only) for tea, soup, and homemade baked goods mid-hike — a classic Banff experience. Budget ~$15–20 CAD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coyotes Southwestern Grill on Caribou Street — fresh, flavourful Southwestern cuisine at mid-range prices. Budget ~$25–40 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most demanding day of the trip — two iconic locations and significant hiking. Wear proper hiking boots, carry 2+ litres of water, sunscreen, and layers. The Plain of Six Glaciers trail gains ~365 metres elevation. Shuttle reservations for Moraine Lake must be booked well in advance via Parks Canada's reservation system. Consider renting a canoe at Lake Louise (~$155 CAD/hour) if you want the full lake experience after your hike.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint. Depart hotel by 8:30 AM and drive north on the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93) — consistently ranked one of the world's most scenic drives. First stop: Bow Lake viewpoint (~55 km north of Banff) for stunning glacier and lake views. Continue to Peyto Lake Viewpoint (~75 km north) — hike the short Bow Summit trail (1.6 km return, easy) to the viewpoint where the wolf-head-shaped lake glows an electric turquoise. Allow 30–45 minutes here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north on the Parkway to the Columbia Icefield area (~125 km from Banff). Stop at the Athabasca Glacier viewpoint for photos and a walk to the glacier toe (free, 30 minutes). Optionally take the Ice Explorer tour onto the glacier (~$65 CAD, book in advance). Begin the return drive south, stopping at Sunwapta Falls (~175 km from Banff) for a short 10-minute walk to the dramatic canyon waterfall. Arrive back in Banff by approximately 5:30–6:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Banff. Visit the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity campus for a peaceful walk with mountain views, or simply stroll along the Bow River pathway at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from Nesters Market to enjoy at a Parkway pullout — Bow Lake is a perfect picnic spot with a stunning backdrop.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse on Banff Avenue — a mid-range steakhouse with Alberta beef. Budget ~$40–60 CAD per person for a treat after a big driving day.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your gas tank before leaving Banff — there are very limited fuel stops along the Parkway. Download an offline map as cell service is sporadic. Bring a jacket even in summer; temperatures at the Columbia Icefield are significantly colder than Banff. The full round-trip drive is approximately 250 km and takes 8–9 hours with stops.

day_by_day.morning: Lighter activity day — hike the Tunnel Mountain Trail, a short but rewarding hike right from town (4.8 km return, moderate, ~90 minutes). Starting near the hotel area, the trail climbs through Douglas fir forest to the summit of Tunnel Mountain (1,690 m) with sweeping 360° views of the Bow Valley, Mt. Rundle, and the Banff townsite. Perfect for a relaxed morning without needing to drive far.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (mid-range admission ~$10 CAD) to learn about the cultural and natural history of the Rockies. Spend 1–1.5 hours exploring. Afterwards, rent bikes from Soul Ski & Bike or Banff Adventures (~$15–25 CAD/hour) and cycle the Bow River Legacy Trail — a paved multi-use path stretching 26 km between Banff and Canmore along the river valley. Cycle as far as you like and return at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a relaxing spa treatment at the hotel or at the Willow Stream Spa at the Fairmont Banff Springs (day pass available, ~$60–80 CAD). End the evening with a casual dinner and some souvenir shopping along Banff Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or visit Evelyn's Coffee Bar on Banff Avenue for coffee and a breakfast sandwich — a local favourite.
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Grizzly House on Banff Avenue — a Banff institution since 1967, known for fondue and wild game. A fun mid-range experience. Budget ~$30–45 CAD per person.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Banff Ave Brewing Co. — local craft beers and pub-style comfort food in a relaxed atmosphere. Budget ~$20–35 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is intentionally lighter to rest legs after the demanding earlier days. The Tunnel Mountain hike is beginner-friendly and great for sunrise or early morning light. The Legacy Trail cycling is flat and paved — suitable for all fitness levels. Check bike rental availability in advance on busy summer weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — rise early for a peaceful sunrise walk along the Bow River Pathway from the hotel. Walk across the Bow Falls footbridge to view Bow Falls (a short, easy 20-minute walk from downtown). Take in the Banff townsite one last time with the morning light on Mt. Rundle. Return to the hotel for breakfast and begin packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (standard checkout 11:00 AM — confirm with hotel). Before departing, make one final stop at Two Jack Lake (~13 km from Banff) for a serene last look at the Rockies reflected in a quiet, less-crowded lake — a beautiful and peaceful farewell to Banff. Then begin the 1.5-hour drive back to Calgary International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive, parking/shuttle, and airport check-in. Grab a final Alberta meal at the airport if time allows.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the hotel or at Bear Street Tavern — eggs Benedict and coffee with a mountain view to close out the trip.
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snacks packed from Nesters Market to enjoy on the drive back to Calgary, or stop in Canmore (~20 minutes from Banff) at Communitea Café for a healthy, relaxed farewell meal. Budget ~$15–25 CAD per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Calgary International or en route depending on flight time.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm hotel checkout time in advance and arrange luggage storage if needed for the Two Jack Lake visit. Fuel up the rental car before returning it in Calgary. Two Jack Lake is a short detour off the Trans-Canada and well worth the 30-minute stop — it's quieter than Lake Louise and equally beautiful for a final reflection. Keep your Parks Canada pass handy — it's valid all day.

day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Banff (45 min) and freshen up at the lodge before a fine dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — request a packed trail lunch from the lodge kitchen
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse — a historic alpine teahouse serving homemade soups, sandwiches, and baked goods; all supplies are carried in by horse, making it a truly unique dining experience
meals.dinner: Eden Restaurant at Rimrock Resort Hotel, Banff — AAA Four Diamond fine dining with an exceptional tasting menu, award-winning wine cellar, and panoramic mountain views

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Lake Louise parking lot no later than 7:30 AM; it fills completely by 9:00 AM in July. Alternatively, take the Parks Canada shuttle from the Park & Ride in Lake Louise village. Wear layers — temperatures at the teahouse elevation can be 8–10°C cooler than the valley. Canoe rentals are first-come, first-served so aim to paddle mid-afternoon when hikers return.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake — Valley of the Ten Peaks Trail — Depart at 6:00 AM sharp (Moraine Lake Road is access-controlled in 2027; a timed-entry reservation or shuttle is mandatory). Hike the Rockpile Trail for the world-famous panoramic view of Moraine Lake framed by the Ten Peaks, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail for intimate close-up perspectives of the glacially fed lake. The vivid blue-green colour is at its most intense in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return via shuttle to Lake Louise village. Stop at the Lake Louise Ski Resort area for a scenic gondola ride (optional) or relax at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise's Lakeview Lounge with afternoon tea before driving back to Banff.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the terrace at the Banff Mountain Lodge, followed by dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed gourmet breakfast box from the lodge (arrange the night before) — enjoy at Moraine Lake's lakeshore
meals.lunch: Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise — Lakeview Lounge afternoon tea or the Walliser Stube Wine Bar for Swiss-inspired charcuterie boards and Alpine fondue
meals.dinner: Juniper Bistro, Banff — contemporary Canadian cuisine with locally sourced ingredients and stunning panoramic views of Mount Norquay and the Bow Valley from its hillside perch

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake Road is closed to private vehicles in peak season 2027 — book the Roam Transit shuttle or a Parks Canada timed-entry permit well in advance (reservations open in April). Bring a warm mid-layer as mornings at Moraine Lake (1,885 m) can be crisp. Wildlife sightings (grizzly bear, elk, hoary marmot) are common — carry bear spray and know how to use it.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — Drive 26 km west of Banff to Johnston Canyon (30-min drive). Walk the dramatic catwalk trail bolted into the canyon walls above the rushing creek, passing through narrow limestone gorges to the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). For the adventurous, continue to the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs with vivid turquoise and green pools (5.8 km one way, highly recommended).
day_by_day.afternoon: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk — Return to Banff and ride the Banff Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain (2,281 m). Stroll the 1 km summit boardwalk connecting to Sanson Peak, enjoying 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges. Visit the restored Cosmic Ray Station, a National Historic Site at the summit.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a signature spa treatment at the Willow Stream Spa at the Fairmont Banff Springs (book in advance), followed by a celebratory dinner at the iconic hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch at the Ink Pots or Johnston Canyon — arrange a premium charcuterie and cheese box from Nourish Bistro or the hotel
meals.dinner: 1888 Chop House at the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel — premium Alberta steaks, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine list inside the legendary 'Castle in the Rockies'; a truly bucket-list dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is best visited on a weekday morning to avoid crowds — arrive by 8:00 AM. The catwalk can be slippery; wear trail shoes with grip. The Banff Gondola last ride up is typically 9:00 PM in July, so the afternoon/early evening timing allows for golden-hour views from the summit. Book Willow Stream Spa at least 2–3 weeks in advance for peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Peyto Lake — Depart Banff by 7:30 AM for the world-renowned Icefields Parkway (Highway 93). Drive north, stopping at Bow Lake (stunning turquoise glacial lake with the Num-Ti-Jah Lodge as backdrop) for a short lakeshore walk. Continue to the Peyto Lake Viewpoint — hike the 2.2 km Bow Summit Loop Trail to the elevated viewpoint where Peyto Lake's extraordinary wolf-head shape and electric blue colour are revealed in full glory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre. Take the Ice Explorer tour onto the Athabasca Glacier — ride massive all-terrain vehicles onto the surface of one of the most accessible glaciers in North America. Optionally add the Skywalk (glass-floored cliff-edge walkway over the Sunwapta Valley). Begin the scenic return drive south along the Parkway, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by 7:00–7:30 PM. Enjoy a relaxed final full-day dinner with wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the long drive
meals.lunch: Num-Ti-Jah Lodge at Bow Lake — rustic-elegant lakeside dining with homemade soups and sandwiches; a perfect mid-drive stop with one of the most beautiful views in the Rockies
meals.dinner: Saltlik Steakhouse, Banff — award-winning prime Alberta beef, premium sides, and an impressive whisky and wine selection in a warm, upscale atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Icefields Parkway is 230 km one way — this is a full-day excursion (10–12 hours with stops). Fill your gas tank in Banff before departing; fuel is very limited along the Parkway. Book the Columbia Icefield Ice Explorer tour online in advance to secure your preferred time slot. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a warm jacket — temperatures on the glacier surface can be near freezing even in July.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a peaceful sunrise walk along the Bow River Trail from the town centre (flat, easy, 5 km loop) to reflect on the week's adventures. Visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a luxurious soak in the historic thermal mineral pools on Sulphur Mountain's lower slopes — the perfect physical recovery after a week of hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse Banff Avenue's premium boutiques for Canadian artisan souvenirs, Indigenous art, and outdoor gear. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for a cultural immersion into the history and art of the mountain west. Enjoy a leisurely final lunch before checking out of the hotel and beginning the private transfer back to Calgary International Airport (depart Banff by 3:00–3:30 PM to allow ample time for check-in).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary International Airport — or, if the flight is the following morning, enjoy a final dinner in Calgary's vibrant 17th Avenue dining district.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the hotel — savour the full lodge experience one last time
meals.lunch: The Bison Restaurant & Terrace, Banff — farm-to-table Canadian cuisine in a warm, rustic-chic setting; renowned for Alberta bison dishes, wild game, and an excellent brunch/lunch menu
meals.dinner: If departing late or staying in Calgary: Vin Room on 17th Ave (wine bar with exceptional small plates) or River Café on Prince's Island Park (iconic Calgary fine dining)

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time at most Banff hotels is 11:00 AM — arrange a late check-out (12:00–1:00 PM) with the lodge if needed to allow time for the hot springs visit. The Banff Upper Hot Springs opens at 9:00 AM; arrive early before the midday rush. Allow at least 1.5–2 hours for the Banff-to-Calgary drive under normal conditions, plus extra time in July for potential wildlife or construction delays on the Trans-Canada Highway.
